author: product-requirements-expert
title: Specialty view of the veterinarian directory
summary: A read-only specialty view of the directory: it lists every specialty by its stored name, each with the veterinarians who hold it, shown by full name (first name then last name). A veterinarian holding no specialty does not appear. All specialties render together on one page, no pagination.
acceptance_criteria: Given the clinic's specialties, when the specialty view is opened, then every specialty is listed by its stored name, each with the veterinarians who hold it
Given a veterinarian who holds a specialty, when the specialty view is opened, then that veterinarian is shown by full name, first name then last name (for example "Helen Leary")
Given a veterinarian who holds no specialty, when the specialty view is opened, then that veterinarian does not appear on it
Given the clinic's specialties, when the specialty view is opened, then all specialties appear together on one page, with no pagination
The specialties, and the veterinarians under each, are presented in a stable order rather than an arbitrary one
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or their specialties through the application stays out of scope (NG-2 unchanged); the specialty view is read-only
notes: Product owner specified the concrete surface as GET /specialties.html, mirroring the existing /vets.html directory; the exact route is a design detail carried here so it is not lost. This is the inverse projection of the same cached veterinarian collection VetRepository.findAll() already returns — grouping by Specialty is a presentation concern. Navigation/landing-page links to the new page were not requested and are left out of this slice.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The specialty view is the inverse projection of the existing vet directory and belongs in the vet feature package, reusing the established repository->controller->Thymeleaf pattern (system-design.md#contracts, #server-side-rendering ADR). Add a read route to the existing VetController and a new template under templates/vets/; the only new element is a presentation-side inversion that groups the cached vet collection by specialty. No new module, repository, dependency, or persisted type. system-design.md Contracts rows for Vet, Specialty, VetRepository, and VetController updated to add REQ-VET-003.
integration_points: Add GET /specialties.html to VetController (the product-named surface, mirroring /vets.html), returning view name vets/specialtyList; keep it on the same controller since specialties are the inverse of the vet directory in the same feature package

Data source is the existing unpaged, cached vetRepository.findAll() (Collection<Vet>) — no new repository method and no SpecialtyRepository; there is none in the codebase, so specialties are derived by inverting the vet collection
No pagination: render every specialty together on one page (AC4). Do not add a paged findAll variant

Invert the vet collection into specialty->veterinarians in the controller (a private helper), optionally via a small package-private immutable projection record (e.g. specialty name + its ordered vets) to keep the inversion understandable and the model attribute clean; expose it as a single model attribute for the template
Template mirrors vetList.html: same layout fragment layout(~{::body},'vets') so the active nav tab stays 'vets'; drop the pagination block entirely

Vets are shown by full name first-then-last exactly as vetList.html formats them (${vet.firstName + ' ' + vet.lastName}); specialty names render from stored data (${specialty.name}), not from message keys

patterns.description: existing showVetList read route + model + Thymeleaf view-name pattern to mirror
getSpecialties() already sorts specialties by name — reuse the same by-name ordering for the specialty axis

MockMvc @WebMvcTest with @MockitoBean VetRepository; the four theSpecialtyViewShould... tests follow showVetListHtml, stubbing findAll() to return vets whose specialties invert into the expected grouping, and asserting view name + model attribute

risks.risk: AC5/edge-case-2 require stable ordering of specialties AND of the veterinarians under each; the raw findAll() Collection and Set<Specialty> membership are unordered
risks.mitigation: Order specialties by stored name (consistent with Vet.getSpecialties()); order veterinarians under each by a deterministic key such as last name then first name. Both orderings must be explicit in the assembly code, not incidental to collection iteration

risks.risk: AC/PRD wording 'every specialty the clinic recognises' could be read as every Specialty row including one held by no vet; deriving from findAll() omits any unheld specialty
risks.mitigation: The prd-entry fixes the mechanism as the inverse projection of VetRepository.findAll(), and the current seed (vet_specialties rows map every specialty 1/2/3 to a vet) makes the two readings identical — the omission is unobservable. Implement the projection as specified; if a future seed adds an unheld specialty and it must appear, that needs a SpecialtyRepository and is a new slice, not this one

risks.risk: REQ-LANG-002: no hard-coded user-facing text, and every message key present in all 11 locale bundles
risks.mitigation: Reuse the existing 'specialties' key (present in all 11 bundles) for the page heading; specialty names and vet names are data, not chrome. If any NEW user-facing label is introduced, add it to all 11 files under src/main/resources/messages/ or the build-time bundle-parity test fails

notes: Verdict minor, not covered: reuses the vet-directory pattern but adds a new route, a new template, and a presentation-side inversion (a thin new layer). No ADR — /specialties.html is a product-named detail carried in the prd-entry, and controller-side grouping vs a projection record is a small implementation choice with no hard-to-reverse trade-off. Navigation/landing-page links are out of scope per the prd-entry (NG unchanged; this is read-only, NG-2 intact). Caching: reuses @Cacheable("vets") findAll(); read-only, adds no new cache and does not affect the open vet-cache-invalidation question. No design-doc-autofix records to audit since no prior design-block for this req_id.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The specialty view belongs in the vet feature package, reusing the established repository->controller->Thymeleaf pattern (system-design.md#contracts, #server-side-rendering ADR). CORRECTION to the superseded block: the data source for the specialty axis is the STORED specialty set, not an inversion of vetRepository.findAll(). PRD line 128 (REQ-VET-003 acceptance criterion) governs 'the clinic's specialties' = the stored set; deriving specialties by inverting findAll() omits any specialty held by no veterinarian, which contradicts the recorded criterion (not merely latent). Specialty is a standalone @Entity backed by the specialties table (src/main/java/.../vet/Specialty.java, seeded in db/*/data.sql), so the stored set is directly readable. Add a thin read-only SpecialtyRepository alongside VetRepository as the specialty axis; the vets under each specialty are still supplied by the existing cached vetRepository.findAll(). Read-only throughout; NG-2 (no vet write path) unchanged. system-design.md Contracts updated: VetRepository row reworded, new SpecialtyRepository row added, VetController row reworded.
integration_points: Add GET /specialties.html to VetController (the product-named surface, mirroring /vets.html), returning view name vets/specialtyList; keep it on the same controller since the specialty view is the other face of the vet directory in the same feature package

NEW read-only repository: SpecialtyRepository extends Repository<Specialty,Integer> with a single @Transactional(readOnly=true) findAll() returning Collection<Specialty>. Mirror the shape of owner/PetTypeRepository (the existing read-only lookup repository). This is the specialty axis: every stored specialty renders, including one held by no veterinarian (empty vet list under it). Do NOT add a write method and do NOT add it to the vets cache; leaving it uncached is fine (lookup-set read on a rarely-hit page)

Data assembly in the controller (a private helper): read the stored specialties from specialtyRepository.findAll() as the primary axis; iterate the cached vetRepository.findAll() to attach, under each specialty, the vets that hold it (Vet.getSpecialties() membership). Expose one model attribute — a small package-private immutable projection (specialty name + its ordered vets) per specialty keeps the template clean
No pagination: render every stored specialty together on one page (AC4, PRD line 128). Do not add a paged variant

Template mirrors vetList.html: same layout fragment layout(~{::body},'vets') so the active nav tab stays 'vets'; drop the pagination block entirely. Specialty names render from stored data (specialty.name), vets by full name first-then-last exactly as vetList.html formats them (vet.firstName + ' ' + vet.lastName)

If any NEW user-facing label is introduced, add it to all 11 bundle files or the build-time bundle-parity test fails

notes: Supersedes line 4 at root's human-checkpoint-2 intervention. CORRECTION: the superseded block treated the omission of an unheld specialty as 'latent, unobservable' and pinned the mechanism to inverting findAll(); that reading contradicts the REQ-VET-003 acceptance criterion (PRD line 128, 'the clinic's specialties' = the stored set), so it is corrected, not deferred. The current seed (specialties radiology/surgery/dentistry, all held via vet_specialties) makes the two readings coincide TODAY, but the design now conforms to the criterion regardless of seed. The 'veterinarian holding no specialty does not appear' criterion STILL HOLDS under the new data source: the grouping is built by attaching vets to stored specialties, so a vet with no specialty is attached to none and never appears. Verdict remains minor: adds a new route, a new template, a thin read-only repository mirroring PetTypeRepository, and a presentation-side join — an existing pattern with a small adjustment, no hard-to-reverse trade-off, no ADR. NG-2 intact (read-only, no vet/specialty write path). Caching: SpecialtyRepository adds no new cache and does not touch the open vet-cache-invalidation question (system-design.md Open Questions #5). No design-doc-autofix records to audit since the superseded design-block.

findings.description: veterinariansHolding joins specialties by name equality (held.getName().equals(specialty.getName())) rather than by ID. Names are unique today, but the correct structural join for two Specialty objects loaded from the same schema is by primary key. A future reader will not know whether name-uniqueness is a DB constraint or an assumption. Use held.getId().equals(specialty.getId()) — the IDs are populated by Spring Data from the same rows the name comes from.
findings.fix: Replace held.getName().equals(specialty.getName()) with held.getId().equals(specialty.getId()) in the filter lambda of veterinariansHolding.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: Bare integer literals passed as entity IDs to specialty() and vet() factory calls in all five new test bodies (values 1, 2, 3, 4). These IDs have no bearing on any assertion and are Tier 3 mystery values per the Three-Tier Data Naming Convention in docs/testing-principles.md. Irrelevant required-by-API values belong in Tier 2: declare a single SOME_ID constant (e.g. private static final int SOME_ID = 0) and use it in every factory call, or add auto-incrementing ID generation inside the factory methods themselves so callers never supply an ID.
findings.fix: Declare `private static final int SOME_ID = 0;` at class level and replace every bare integer ID argument in specialty() and vet() calls with SOME_ID, or remove the id parameter from the factory methods and generate it internally.

findings.description: The production code sorts veterinarians under each specialty by Comparator.comparing(Person::getLastName).thenComparing(Person::getFirstName). No test exercises the thenComparing(Person::getFirstName) leg: every test uses vets with distinct last names, so the second comparator key is never verified. PRD edge case 2 requires stable ordering of vets under each specialty. A vet pair sharing a last name but differing on first name (e.g. vet with firstName=Jane lastName=Adams before vet with firstName=Robert lastName=Adams) is needed to verify the full ordering rule.

The @BeforeEach setup() stubs vets.findAll() (no-arg) with james() and helen(), but every new specialty test immediately overrides that stub with its own given(this.vets.findAll()).willReturn(...). The @BeforeEach stub is silently dead code for all five new tests and misleads the next reader into believing it governs them. Move the no-arg vets.findAll() stub into the two pre-existing tests that actually use it (showVetListHtml, showResourcesVetList), leaving @BeforeEach to stub only the paged findAll(any(Pageable.class)) variant that is truly shared.
findings.fix: Remove the given(this.vets.findAll()).willReturn(Lists.newArrayList(james(), helen())); line from @BeforeEach and add it directly inside showVetListHtml and showResourcesVetList.
